source.title: Intergenerational transmission of emotional trauma through amygdala-dependent mother-to-infant transfer of specific fear
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: Direct biological warrant for the design premise ARC-047 rests on but does not defend: that an animal's affective state leaks involuntarily into the world as a diffusible chemical signal, and that a conspecific can acquire a specific affective response from that signal alone. The decisive control is that maternal presence was not required -- the odour of the frightened mother, paired with a novel cue, was sufficient. That is precisely the semi-involuntary scent-emission model ARC-047 specifies, validated in biology rather than assumed from design convenience. Held at 0.68 because it is a rat mother-infant preparation with one alarm channel, and ARC-047 posits seven channels among peer agents, which is a substantial extrapolation.
failure_signatures: A design in which affective broadcast is voluntary or gated by the emitter cannot reproduce this result -- the transmission here runs through an emission the frightened animal does not choose to make.

If the receiving agent must observe the emitter to acquire the response, the mechanism is behavioural imitation and not chemosignalling; this paper's maternal-absence control specifically rules that reading out, so a REE scent channel that only works while the emitter is in view is modelling something else.

The transferred response was specific to the paired cue rather than a diffuse elevation of arousal, so a scent channel implemented as an undifferentiated alarm scalar cannot support the specific-fear acquisition this mechanism produces.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Rat pups acquire an aversion to a specific odour after exposure to their mother expressing fear to that odour; the transfer is amygdala-dependent, involves the Grueneberg ganglion's role in alarm chemosignalling, and maternal presence was not needed -- elevation of the pups' corticosterone induced by the odour of the frightened mother, together with a novel peppermint odour, was sufficient to produce subsequent aversion to that odour.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-047's load-bearing and undefended design assumption is that affective state should leak into the environment involuntarily, as a graded field other agents can read, rather than being emitted as a deliberate communicative act. It lists wanting, seeking, harm_stress and direction as automatic and proportional to internal state, with only defence as a chosen action. This paper is biological warrant for that architecture: a frightened animal emits an alarm chemosignal it does not choose to emit, that signal propagates independently of the emitter's presence, and a receiver acquires a specific affective response from it. It supports MECH-041 (affective expression as mode broadcast) having a real biological referent and supports the specific decision to make the harm_stress and alarm channels involuntary. It also supports the graded-field rendering: a diffusible chemical signal is intrinsically a concentration gradient, which is what ARC-047's Gaussian scent fields are modelling.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The extrapolation is large in three directions and each should be held separately. (1) This is a mother-infant dyad with a strong asymmetry and a developmental window; ARC-047 posits symmetric peer agents, and nothing here shows peer-to-peer transfer works the same way. (2) It is one channel -- alarm -- and ARC-047 posits seven simultaneous ones including wanting, seeking, celebration and direction, for which this paper is no evidence at all; alarm chemosignalling is the best-attested of the seven and the others are being carried by it. (3) The receiver mechanism is amygdala-dependent associative conditioning, not the inferential other-modelling ARC-010 and MECH-031 describe -- the pup is not tagging the mother as a selflike other and interpreting her state, it is being conditioned. That distinction is exactly what ARC-047's harness is supposed to test, so this paper supplies the emission half of the design and nothing of the interpretation half.
mapping.source_context: Rat mother-infant preparation; mothers fear-conditioned to peppermint odour pre-partum, pups exposed to the mother's fear expression or to the odour of a frightened mother in her absence; measures included pup odour aversion, corticosterone, and lateral and basal amygdala activity.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: PNAS, a clean dissociation design, and the maternal-absence condition is the control that makes the chemosignalling interpretation stick rather than a behavioural-observation one. Mapping fidelity moderate -- it validates the emission side of ARC-047's design precisely and the reception side not at all. Transfer risk is the highest in this batch and is where most of the discount sits: rat mother-infant alarm chemosignalling to seven-channel peer affective leakage in a gridworld is a long way, and it is being asked to carry six channels it never tested.
